cards.title: Small deterministic parsimonious universal families
cards.formal: Can small δ-parsimonious universal families be constructed deterministically, matching the desired leading exponential dependence on k=p+q? In the balanced case p=q=k/2, the source specifically seeks size 2^{k+o(k)} in place of the cited deterministic 4^{k+o(k)} scale. The family must give nearly the same positive number of separations for every disjoint pair of a p-set and a q-set, and supply its correction factor. The source suppresses dependence on n and δ in this comparison and leaves the deterministic resource target implicit, so the complete joint-parameter construction claim remains to be specified.
cards.why: Would make uniform multiplicity control available as an explicit combinatorial tool for deterministic approximate counting, beyond the specially structured pairs used in the existing path algorithm.
cards.status_note: Read the exact family definition, random construction and its indexing convention, and the deterministic section in both the conference and full versions. Subsequent searches through 12 September 2026 did not locate a general construction meeting the intended size scale. The exact n/δ regime and deterministic resource bounds remain unspecified in the extracted question.

progress.text: Randomized small families and deterministic restricted families are established; the general small deterministic construction is left open.
The TALG full article retains the unrestricted question and develops the nice-pair relaxation in detail.

cards.review_note: The source explicitly contrasts balanced-case sizes 4^{k+o(k)} and 2^{k+o(k)}, but leaves dependence on universe size n and accuracy δ suppressed in that sentence. It does not fix the permitted deterministic construction time, enumeration delay or workspace for the general family. No arbitrary bound such as exactly matching the randomized output-linear time is imposed here.

sentences: A universal family separates every disjoint p-set and q-set in an n-element universe.
Parsimony additionally requires approximately the same number of family entries to separate each pair.
The desired deterministic size has leading scale 2^k for balanced pairs, where k=p+q.
The source supplies a random construction and a deterministic relaxation for selected pairs, rather than the general construction.
The suppressed universe-size and accuracy dependence, along with deterministic resource bounds, still need specification.

cards.definitions: Let U=[n]={1,…,n}, with positive integers p,q and k=p+q≤n, and let 0<δ<1 be an accuracy parameter. For a finite indexed collection F=(F₁,…,Fₜ) of subsets of U, define N_F(A,B)=|{j∈[t]: A⊆Fⱼ and B∩Fⱼ=∅}|. The collection is δ-parsimonious if a single positive correction factor T satisfies (1−δ)T≤N_F(A,B)≤(1+δ)T for every pair of disjoint sets A,B⊆U with |A|=p and |B|=q. In particular every such pair is separated at least once, since its integer count is strictly positive. T is the same for all pairs and must be provided with the family. Counting is by entries, as in the source’s independently generated indexed family; repeated entries cannot simply be discarded while preserving these counts. An entry may be represented by its n-bit membership vector. The deterministic construction task receives n,p,q and a finite representation of δ, and must produce the family and a usable representation of T with no failure probability. The number of entries, total construction time, delay between emitted entries and working memory are separate resources. For p=q=k/2, k is even and tends to infinity; o(k) denotes a function whose ratio to k tends to zero, once the dependence of n and δ on k has been specified. An ordinary universal family guarantees only N_F(A,B)≥1 and allows unbounded variation in those counts. A construction that works only on selected pairs does not satisfy this definition for all pairs.
cards.answer_criterion: Under a fully specified joint parameter regime and deterministic resource bounds, construct a family and correction factor meeting the near-uniform separation inequalities for every disjoint pair and the stated size bound, or prove that this construction requirement is impossible. An ordinary universal family, a randomized construction, or a family satisfying the inequalities only for the paper’s selected nice pairs does not settle the unrestricted target. Suppressed universe-size/accuracy dependence and deterministic resource bounds must be fixed before this can serve as a complete benchmark proposition.

context_blocks.title: Parsimony controls counting distortion
context_blocks.text: Coverage alone is enough to locate a witness, but counting through many separations can count different witnesses different numbers of times. A common correction factor with relative error δ limits that distortion.

context_blocks.title: Small families exist with random construction
context_blocks.text: The source constructs an indexed family of size O((k^k/(p^p q^q))k log n·δ⁻²) in O(tn) time for t entries, with success probability at least 1−n^{−100k}. In the balanced case the leading ratio is 2^k. This includes n and δ factors omitted from the later shorthand comparison.

context_blocks.title: The deterministic counting algorithm uses a relaxation
context_blocks.text: The full article repeats the desired balanced-case size improvement, then defines a family for nice pairs satisfying additional compatibility conditions. Its deterministic path-counting theorem uses that relaxation and does not assert a general parsimonious universal-family construction.

cards.context:
Coverage alone is enough to locate a witness, but counting through many separations can count different witnesses different numbers of times. A common correction factor with relative error δ limits that distortion.

The source constructs an indexed family of size O((k^k/(p^p q^q))k log n·δ⁻²) in O(tn) time for t entries, with success probability at least 1−n^{−100k}. In the balanced case the leading ratio is 2^k. This includes n and δ factors omitted from the later shorthand comparison.

The full article repeats the desired balanced-case size improvement, then defines a family for nice pairs satisfying additional compatibility conditions. Its deterministic path-counting theorem uses that relaxation and does not assert a general parsimonious universal-family construction.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
